description: Move Web and runner lifecycle push delivery out of durable CloudEvent dispatch while preserving authoritative state reconciliation.

tasks.title: Deliver bounded best-effort Web event push
tasks.description: Add the bounded in-process event-push queue, worker, and distinct push-handler registration path. Migrate the Web EventBridge to this path while preserving subscriber filtering and its existing CloudEvent envelope, and remove it from durable subscription/dead-letter participation.
acceptanceCriteria: A persisted domain event is non-blockingly offered to the bounded push queue without awaiting Web connection lookup or SignalR delivery from EventDispatcherService.
Queue saturation, connection lookup failure, handler failure, and send timeout are logged as best-effort outcomes and cannot retry, block source ordering, or create a durable-dispatch dead letter.
The push worker receives TimeProvider and applies the configured delivery timeout through a TimeProvider-backed cancellation token passed to each handler.
Subscribed Web connections continue to receive the existing OnEvent CloudEvent envelope and unsubscribed connections receive no event.

Focused server tests cover queue admission/drop, worker failure containment, FakeTimeProvider-driven timeout cancellation with an awaitable worker signal, Web fan-out preservation, and the absence of EventBridge from the durable subscription collection; the relevant SpecTests project passes.
tasks.output: Bounded event-push infrastructure and Web EventBridge migration with focused server tests.
tasks.notes: Keep the queue process-local and non-persistent. Do not use the unbounded IBackgroundTaskLauncher for per-event push work or wall-clock/scheduler waits for timeout behavior.

tasks.title: Route runner terminal status through event push
tasks.description: Migrate runner terminal workflow-status delivery from its durable subscription to the event-push handler path introduced by T-001. Preserve the existing runner lookup and ReceiveWorkflowRunStatus payload for Completed and Stopped only, while retaining runner polling as recovery for dropped pushes.
acceptanceCriteria: Completed and Stopped workflow events attempt the existing runner status notification only when an assigned runner is connected, without participating in durable retry or dead-letter handling.
Failed workflow events do not emit a terminal runner notification or make a recoverable workspace cleanup-eligible.
Disconnected runners, router errors, SignalR failures, and FakeTimeProvider-driven timeout cancellation are contained as best-effort outcomes and do not delay or retry the source workflow event.

Focused server tests cover connected delivery payloads, offline and send-failure isolation, Failed exclusion, removal of the legacy durable handler expectation, and runner status-poll reconciliation; the relevant SpecTests project passes.
tasks.output: Runner terminal-status push migration with regression coverage for lifecycle and reconciliation behavior.
tasks.notes: Do not change the status polling endpoint, runner workspace policy, or SignalR wire payload.
